records.summary: Rewrote the 10.1 AI/ML scale-up sequence diagram in both locales. records.summary: The write-pipeline pseudocode read the dedup marker only by (tenant, source, event_id) and rejected only strictly-older source_version, so a different event_id carrying the same (tenant, source, entity, version) with a different payload fell into the upsert branch and could overwrite already-published history; the marker's digest check also did not bind envelope/version. The transactional-outbox guidance (at-least-once delivery requires idempotent, dedup-tracked consumers; FIFO for exactly-once+ordering) supports making exact retries idempotent and conflicting envelopes rejected. records.summary: The 'Conventional L7 limitations' section asserted universally that Round-Robin neutralizes prefix cache and that L7 gateways cannot see tokens/streaming/model metrics, treating a separate inference-routing tier as mandatory. Each limitation (both locales) is rescoped to an UNCONFIGURED, request-count-only balancer rather than L7 gateways inherently: an unconfigured round-robin lowers (not neutralizes) prefix-cache reuse, and when multiple replicas are already warmed with the same prefix, reuse still occurs under round-robin, so the effect depends on replica count and cache holdings. The problem is framed as a cache-locality vs. load-balancing tradeoff with two options to tune it — a separate inference routing layer (Tier 2 ①) OR adding ext-proc / prefix-scorer plugins to an existing L7 gateway — instead of a mandatory separate tier. Token/streaming awareness is noted as an optional plugin/ext-proc capability. Heading was not renamed.

records.summary: On the English and Korean cache-hit strategy, KV cache optimization and llm-d on EKS Auto Mode pages, round-robin routing is no longer said to neutralize prefix-cache reuse or to be what every existing vLLM deployment uses. The pages now separate two mechanisms: Automatic Prefix Caching is kept per vLLM instance (enabled by default in the vLLM v0.25.0 engine configuration) and reuses an earlier request's KV blocks regardless of how the request was routed, while the load balancer decides which instance's cache a request can use. A cache-unaware policy such as round-robin therefore dilutes locality, because each replica that receives a prefix computes it once and keeps it alongside other traffic, rather than eliminating reuse; the extent depends on the number of replicas and distinct prefixes, the cache capacity and the configured traffic distribution. The llm-d overview names round-robin as the baseline of llm-d's published comparison and makes the benefit conditional on reusable prefixes, load and the scorers of the optimized-baseline configuration (a prefix-cache scorer with KV-cache-utilization and queue-size scorers), and the KV cache page describes llm-d and NVIDIA Dynamo as estimating or tracking which Pods hold a prefix and weighing that against load.
